chunks: Abū ‘Abdillāh Muḥammad ibn Aḥmad ibn Ya’qūb narrated to me from ‘Ali ibn Ḥasan ibn ‘Ali ibn Faḍḍāl, from his father, from some of our companions, from one of the Imams (peace be upon him), who said:

Verily Allāh, the Blessed and the Exalted, created Ādam (peace be upon him) from clay, so He forbade clay upon his offspring. I asked, 'What do you say about the clay of the grave of al-Ḥusayn (peace be upon him)?' He replied, 'It is unlawful for people to eat their own flesh, but it is permissible for them to eat our flesh; however, a small amount of it is permissible, like a chickpea.'

key_terms.قَبْرِ الْحُسَيْنِ (ص): grave of al-Husayn (peace be upon him)

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to eat the clay from the grave of Imam al-Husayn?
ai.summary: In Kamil al-Ziyarat, Ibn Qulawayh records this hadith to establish the permissibility of consuming the clay of the Imams' graves as a form of spiritual cure (shifa) and barakah. The Imam distinguishes this from the general prohibition of eating earth, likening the clay to the Imams' own flesh—permissible yet distinct from human sustenance—and specifies that only a small quantity, such as a chickpea, is consumed. This practice underscores the Shia belief in the physical holiness of the Imams and the therapeutic value of their remains.

en.sayyid-mohsen-al-husayni-al-milani: 3. Abū ‘Abdillāh Muḥammad ibn Aḥmad ibn Ya’qūb narrated to me from ‘Ali ibn Ḥasan ibn ‘Ali ibn Faďďāl, from his father, from some of our companions, who said: Abū Ja’far (Imam Bāqir (a.s.)) or Abū ‘Abdillāh (Imam Sādiq (a.s.)) said:

Verily Allāh, the Blessed and the Exalted, created Ādam from clay. Therefore, He forbade (eating) clay on the children of Ādam (mankind). I asked, “What about (eating some of) the clay of the grave of Ḥusain (a.s.)?” Imam (a.s.) replied, “It is unlawful for people to eat their own flesh but is it permissible for them to eat our flesh?!!! It is permissible to eat a very little amount from it, as much as a chick-pea.”
